title: Constant-coefficient tensor calculus for the finite etale exceptional adjoint
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $Y$ over $k$ is assumed. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Use the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F_{f,C}=Rp_{f,*}j_!$, and fix its right adjoint $G_{f,C}$ with counit $\epsilon_C$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. There exists an integer $N_f\ge0$ depending only on $f$, not on $C$, such that, for every integer $a$, $F_{f,C}$ sends $D^{\le a}$ into $D^{\le a+N_f}$, using the standard cohomological bounds [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For any integer $d\ge0$ bounding the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, one can take $N_f=2d$.

For $V\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], write $V_T$ for the termwise constant-sheaf complex on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and use derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor]; no boundedness or perfectness of $V$ is imposed. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the canonical maps
$$V_Y\otimes_C^L F_{f,C}K\longrightarrow F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^L K),\qquad V_X\otimes_C^L G_{f,C}M\longrightarrow G_{f,C}(V_Y\otimes_C^L M)$$
are isomorphisms. The first is the compact-support projection map. The second is its adjunction transpose: its transpose is the composite
$$F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^LG_{f,C}M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{proj}^{-1}}V_Y\otimes_C^LF_{f,C}G_{f,C}M\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_C}V_Y\otimes_C^LM.$$
These are natural transformations on the unbounded derived categories and independent of complex resolutions. The tensor here is by a constant coefficient complex $V$; no analogous assertion for an arbitrary sheaf complex on $Y$ is included.

source.place: Theorem 2.18(2), Corollary 2.19 (printed p. 12), Construction 2.26 and Proposition 2.29(2) (printed pp. 14–16), specialized to schemes over Spec k. Supplies the finite-coefficient tensor input to the adic-stage paragraph of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, so $X,Y,\overline X$ are Noetherian by finite type over a Noetherian base, and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Here $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$: on a finite affine cover of $Y$, take finite affine covers of the inverse images under the finite-type map $p_f$; a finite list of $k$-algebra generators for each base algebra, together with the chosen algebra generators upstairs, generates the upstairs algebra over $k$. Thus this assertion follows directly from the definition of finite type. Choose $d\ge0$ bounding the dimensions of the scheme-theoretic fibres of $f$, using quasi-compactness of $Y$. Extension of the residue field to an algebraic closure preserves the dimension of each finite-type fibre, so the same $d$ bounds the geometric fibres. This choice depends only on $f$. If $X$ or $Y$ is empty choose $d=0$; all compact-support values on an empty source are zero. In the rest of the proof any geometric fibre bound $d$ is allowed, and $N_f=2d$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Tag 0A3V (lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension); quasi-separatedness is Tag 01OY in properties.tex; field-extension invariance is the cited lem-kun-dimension-extension.

proof.text: The termwise $j_!$ is exact and left adjoint to $j^*$, so its functor on the unbounded derived category is exact and preserves arbitrary coproducts. The total derived $Rp_{f,*}$ is exact by the K-injective derived-functor theorem and preserves arbitrary coproducts by the proper coproduct theorem. Thus $F=Rp_{f,*}j_!$ is exact and preserves arbitrary coproducts. Module sheaves have enough injectives; a bounded-below object in $D^{\ge b}$ has a K-injective representative with zero terms below $b$. Applying the additive $p_{f,*}$ termwise to such a representative shows that $Rp_{f,*}$, and therefore $F$, preserves this lower bound. For a sheaf $H$ on $X$, the compact-support cohomological-dimension theorem applies: $C$ is finite and its additive exponent is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. It gives $F(H)\in D^{[0,2d]}$, for arbitrary $H$, with no constructibility assumption.

source.place: Corollary 2.19; unbounded coproducts as in Proposition 2.15. K-injective exactness uses the cited general derived-functor tools.

proof.text: Let $K\in D^{\le a}$. Replace it by a complex with zero terms in degrees $>a$, using good truncation. Its brutal lower subcomplexes $B_m=\sigma_{\ge a-m}K$, $m\ge0$, form an increasing sequence with termwise colimit $K$. Each $B_m$ has a finite filtration by its individual terms in their original degrees, so exactness of $F$ and the sheaf bound of step 2 give $F(B_m)\in D^{\le a+2d}$: at a filtration step the cohomology long exact sequence keeps the upper bound. The complex-colimit theorem identifies $K$ with the telescope of $(B_m)$, and the hocolimit-preservation theorem identifies $F(K)$ with a telescope of $(F(B_m))$. Coproducts are termwise in these derived categories, since module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian; their exactness means that a coproduct of objects in $D^{\le a+2d}$ is still in this subcategory. The telescope triangle and its long exact cohomology sequence therefore give $F(K)\in D^{\le a+2d}$. No convergence assertion for an unbounded spectral sequence is needed. Together with step 2, on bounded intervals this gives $F(D^{[r,s]})\subset D^{[r,s+2d]}$.

source.place: Telescope argument (homotopy colimits); the complex-colimit and exact-functor telescope lemmas cited above.

proof.text:
For any $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ compose the proper projection isomorphism and the open-immersion tensor isomorphism:
$$L\otimes^L Rp_{f,*}j_!K\ \cong\ Rp_{f,*}(p_f^*L\otimes^L j_!K)\ \cong\ Rp_{f,*}j_!(j^*p_f^*L\otimes^L K)=F(f^*L\otimes^L K).$$
Both cited statements apply on the ordinary etale sites to arbitrary unbounded complexes and the given finite commutative ring $C$. The pullbacks here are termwise exact inverse images for the constant coefficient ring. Their composite is $f^*$, and $f^*V_Y=V_X$ because inverse image carries the constant ring and constant-module sheafification to the same constant coefficients. The composite is the compact-support projection map: the proper map is the counit projection map with the indicated tensor symmetries, and the open map is the extension-by-zero tensor map. In particular taking $L=V_Y$ proves the first displayed isomorphism in the statement. We retain the stronger formula for arbitrary $L$ for use in the next step.

source.place: Theorem 2.18(2); equivalently compose the proper and open projection formulas.

proof.text:
Apply the compact-generation lemma to $X$ and $Y$; its hypotheses require finite type over the algebraically closed field and invertibility of $\ell$, not separatedness of either scheme over $k$. Let $(E_s)$ be its family on $X$, and include all integer shifts in the indexing set. To show that $F(E_s)$ is compact, first its cohomology is bounded constructible: the constructible sheaf finiteness theorem applies to each of the finitely many constructible cohomology sheaves of $E_s$, and the successive good-truncation triangles give a finite Postnikov filtration, and exactness of $F$ gives constructibility of $F(E_s)$: the long exact cohomology sequence expresses each new cohomology sheaf as an extension of a kernel and a cokernel of maps between constructible sheaves, which are constructible. Suppose $E_s$ has Tor amplitude $[r,s']$. For every module sheaf $N$ on $Y$, $f^*N$ is a sheaf and step 4 gives
$$F(E_s)\otimes^L N\ \cong\ F(E_s\otimes^L f^*N).$$
The input on the right lies in $D^{[r,s']}$, so steps 2–3 place the output in $D^{[r,s'+2d]}$. Thus $F(E_s)$ has finite Tor amplitude, and compactness on $Y$ follows from the compact-generation lemma. This argument allows nonregular finite rings $C$; no assertion that every finite $C$-module is perfect is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.4.8, with the finite-Tor interpretation of Definition 6.3.1; compact-support constructibility uses the cited finiteness theorem.

proof.text:
The adjunction $F\dashv G$ is the fixed one in the item. The test family $(E_s[n])$ consists of compact objects, detects isomorphisms, and has compact images under $F$ by step 5. All categories have set-indexed coproducts and the required locally small Hom spaces. Apply the compact-test right-adjoint coproduct theorem to conclude that $G$ preserves arbitrary coproducts. Explicitly its comparison $\bigoplus_iGM_i\to G(\bigoplus_iM_i)$ induces, on testing with $E_s[n]$, the isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(FE_s[n],M_i)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}(FE_s[n],\bigoplus_iM_i),$$
by adjunction and compactness of $FE_s[n]$. Detection makes the comparison an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A9R, the Hom-adjunction compactness calculation stated in lem-sc-compact-tests-right-adjoint-coproducts; compactness is Definition 07LS in derived.tex.

proof.text:
Equip $G$ with the unique shift structure compatible with the exact functor $F$ and its fixed adjunction. The adjunction-shift theorem supplies it, with the counit equation
$$\epsilon_{M[n]}=\epsilon_M[n]\circ c_{F,n,GM}\circ F(c_{G,n,M}).$$
The triangulated-right-adjoint theorem then makes $G$ exact with this structure. The constant-complex functor $V\mapsto V_T$ is exact and preserves coproducts: the constant presheaf functor does so sectionwise, and sheafification is exact and preserves all colimits. Passing to complexes preserves shifts and cones; termwise coproducts compute derived coproducts. For fixed $M$ it follows that
$$A_M(V)=V_X\otimes^L GM,\qquad B_M(V)=G(V_Y\otimes^L M)$$
are exact functors of $V\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ and preserve arbitrary coproducts, by the exactness and direct-sum properties of derived tensor and by step 6.

source.place: Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), with the explicitly adjunction-compatible shifts; exactness and sums as in the cited tensor and sheafification lemmas.

proof.text: The projection isomorphism of step 4 is natural, unital and compatible with shifts in the coefficient variable $L$. For the proper factor this is the ringed-topos projection-mate exactness theorem. For the open factor use the canonical extension-by-zero tensor map of the cited open tensor theorem. The extension-by-zero stalk theorem identifies its stalk with the identity where the point lies in $X$ and with $0\to0$ outside $X$; the stalk-tensor theorem identifies the tensor factors. These are equalities on sheaf maps: exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks detect zero morphisms by applying the stalk functors to the image of their difference. Apply this degreewise to complexes. These maps commute with the tensor differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes dy$ and with the usual shift constraints. When factors are interchanged, the symmetry sends $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{\deg x\deg y}y\otimes x$, so the same coefficient-shift square still commutes. The tensor-unit map is the identity under the unit constraints. Composition preserves shift compatibility; thus, denoting step 4's coefficient projection map by $P$, the transformation $P^{-1}_{V,GM}$ commutes with coefficient shifts and has $P^{-1}_{C,GM}=1_{FGM}$ under tensor-unit identifications.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); the open factor uses Tag 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek) in etale-cohomology.tex, with the stated degreewise sign calculation.

proof.text:
Define $\alpha_{V,M}:A_M(V)\to B_M(V)$ by transposing
$$F(V_X\otimes^L GM)\xrightarrow{P^{-1}_{V,GM}}V_Y\otimes^L FGM\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_M}V_Y\otimes^L M.$$
Naturality of $P$, of $\epsilon$, and of the adjunction bijection proves naturality in $V,M$. For completeness the coefficient shift square for $\alpha$ is obtained by transposing its two sides under $F\dashv G$: after using the equation for $\epsilon$ in step 7, the two transposes are precisely the coefficient shift square for $P^{-1}$ from step 8 followed by $1\otimes\epsilon_M$. That square commutes, and the adjunction bijection is injective, so $\alpha$ is compatible with the specified shifts. Under $V=C$, step 8 identifies the transpose with $\epsilon_M$. The adjunction triangle identity says the transpose of $1_{GM}$ is $\epsilon_M$; hence $\alpha_{C,M}=1_{GM}$.

source.place: Construction 2.26, with shift compatibility verified by transposition and the counit equation.

proof.text: Fix $M$ and let $\mathcal L_M$ consist of the coefficient complexes $V$ for which $\alpha_{V,M}$ is invertible. It contains $C$ by step 9. Exactness of both functors and the proved shift compatibility imply that it is closed under shifts, distinguished triangles and retracts by the generating-class invertibility theorem. It is also closed under arbitrary coproducts: under the coproduct comparisons for $A_M$ and $B_M$, naturality along every coprojection identifies $\alpha_{\oplus V_i,M}$ with $\oplus\alpha_{V_i,M}$, which is invertible if each summand is. The derived-module free-generation theorem therefore gives $\mathcal L_M=D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$. Thus the second displayed map in the item is an isomorphism for every unbounded $V$ and $M$. Both maps are constructed from functors, natural maps and the fixed adjunction on the derived categories; changing resolutions computes these same maps, rather than defining a new comparison. This follows for the first map from its proper projection and open tensor construction in step 4, and for the second from the bijectivity of transposition. The argument uses generation only to propagate invertibility, never to infer equality of transformations from their values on generators, and asserts no tensor formula for $G$ with a nonconstant sheaf complex.

One new statement-only compact-generation lemma is needed because existing finite compactness nodes impose the separated standing setting. No smooth purity or SGA route is used.
